cards.text: James is writing to believers he calls his brothers. He's just finished warning rich people who held back the wages of their workers (James 5:4). Now he turns back to the brothers and tells them to be patient until the Lord's coming.

cards.question: James wants to give the brothers a picture of patience they can see. Who does he point to?
The farmer in James's picture is waiting on the precious fruit of the soil. What is he patient for?

cards.text: That farmer can't hurry the rain any more than I can hurry my oven timer. And friend, I have BEGGED that timer. On my knees. It does not negotiate.

cards.question: James tells the brothers that they, too, should be patient and strengthen their hearts. Why?

answers.text: Their hard work will pay off

cards.text: Near, James says. He doesn't give a date, and Jesus said only the Father knows the day (Matthew 24:36), so my job is simple: keep the ovens ready.
Now, waiting gets harder when you're doing it with other people. You ever been stuck in a long line where everybody starts sighing at everybody?

cards.question: While the brothers wait, what does James tell them not to do to one another?
James tells the brothers not to complain about each other, so they won't be judged. Then he adds: "Look, the ___ is standing at the door!"

cards.text: Picture griping about a coworker, then looking up, and the boss is standing RIGHT there in the doorway. Now make it the Judge, and watch how fast my mustache covers my mouth.
Then James gives the brothers some people to look at. He calls them an example of patience in affliction.

cards.question: Who does James give the brothers as an example of patience in affliction?

answers.text: The prophets who spoke in the Lord's name
The kings who ruled over all Israel
The priests who served in the temple

cards.text: James says we consider those who have persevered blessed. Then he names one man the brothers have heard about, a man who lost his flocks, his herds and his children (Job 1:13-19).

cards.question: Which man's perseverance does James remind the brothers about?

cards.text: James reminds them they've seen the outcome the Lord brought for Job. Honestly, I did years in a junk drawer and thought I had it rough, but Job makes my drawer look like a vacation.

cards.question: After bringing up Job, what does James say about the Lord?

answers.text: He is full of compassion and mercy
He helps those who help themselves
He is hard to please but fair

cards.text: Then James says, "Above all, my brothers," and turns to the way they talk.

cards.question: James says not by heaven, not by earth, not by anything else. What does he tell the brothers not to do?
True or false: James says a plain yes or no is enough, so they won't fall under judgment.

cards.text: So no more "I swear on my mustache," friend. Yes means yes, no means no, and that's the whole deal.
Next, James goes mood by mood. Is anyone suffering? He should pray.

cards.question: And if one of the brothers is cheerful, what does James say he should do?

cards.text: Suffering, pray. Cheerful, sing. James just covered every mood I've had today, and I'm only on my SECOND batch.
Next on James's list: anyone who's sick.

cards.question: Who does James say a sick person should call?
True or false: James says the elders should pray over the sick person and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
What does James say the prayer offered in faith will do for the one who is sick?

answers.text: It will show him his sin

cards.question: James says the Lord will raise the sick one up. And if he has sinned? "If he has sinned, he will be ___."

cards.text: So James tells the brothers to confess their sins to each other and pray for each other, so that they may be healed.
To each OTHER, friend. Out loud, to an actual person, like the day I had to admit that the burnt batch hiding behind my oven was mine.

cards.question: What does James say the prayer of a righteous man has?

cards.text: Then James brings up Elijah, a prophet in Israel (1 Kings 17:1). And he points out that Elijah was a man just like us.

cards.question: What did Elijah pray earnestly for?

answers.text: That the sun would stand still

cards.question: After Elijah prayed, how long did it not rain on the land?

cards.text: A man JUST like us. Not a superhero, friend, same as me and you and everybody who's ever hit snooze, and still he prayed and it did not rain.

cards.question: Then Elijah prays again, and James says "the heavens gave ___, and the earth yielded its ___."

cards.text: James has one more thing for the brothers. What if one of them wanders from the truth, and someone brings him back?

cards.question: James says whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will do what?

answers.text: Earn a place among the elders

cards.text: And he'll cover over a multitude of sins. I know what it's like to be brought back out of the dark, friend, so go be somebody's light when the drawer opens.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "Look, the ___ is standing at the door!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "If he has sinned, he will be ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 16 quotes "the heavens gave ___, and the earth yielded its ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: James is the first person to show up, and the card never says who he is. It only says 'James is writing to believers.' It should introduce him simply, with a reference, for example from James 1:1.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the oven timer. It tells no part of the passage, because the farmer's patience was already covered on cards 2 and 3, so it doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card has four sentences: 'That farmer can't hurry…', 'And friend, I have BEGGED that timer.', 'On my knees.' and 'It does not negotiate.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites James 5:9 but tells nothing from that verse. It is only a lead-in comparison about waiting in line, so the citation doesn't match what the card tells and the card tells no part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'Waiting gets harder when you're doing it with other people' links verse 8 to verse 9 as cause and effect. James doesn't make that link.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Travel with one another' isn't a believable warning while the brothers wait for the Lord's coming. It reads as filler, so the right answer is easy to spot.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'He is full of compassion and mercy', sounds like Scripture. The wrong answers sound like modern sayings ('He helps those who help themselves' and 'hard to please but fair'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'Yes means yes, no means no' repeats what card 19 already covered. This is a recap card with a joke and no new passage content.
The wrong answer 'Tell the elders' brings up the elders before card 5 asks who a sick person should call. That hints at card 5's answer, 'The elders of the church'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Suffering, pray. Cheerful, sing.' repeats card 1 and card 2's answer, then adds a joke. It is a recap card that doesn't move the passage forward.
This card restates card 9's instruction ('To each OTHER') and adds a joke, with no new passage content. It also adds 'Out loud', which James 5:16 doesn't say.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card calls Elijah 'a prophet in Israel' and cites 1 Kings 17:1. That verse calls him 'Elijah the Tishbite, from Tishbe in Gilead', not a prophet. A verse that calls him a prophet, such as 1 Kings 18:36, should be cited instead.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: 'A man JUST like us… he prayed and it did not rain' repeats cards 12 to 14 with a joke and adds nothing new from the passage. It is a recap card.

The closing comparison doesn't match the passage's action. Verses 19 and 20 are about bringing back someone who wandered from the truth, but Papa Dorin never wandered; he was forgotten and then called out. 'Go be somebody's light when the drawer opens' also mixes the drawer image with the passage, and a baker would say 'huh?'.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he begged the timer 'On my knees.' He is a cookie stamper who always stands on a gold base, and the docs never say whether he has knees or can kneel.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin describe himself kneeling or 'on my knees', given that his body is a stamper on a gold base he never leaves?
